newsitem.title: USA: Alumax's 96 more challenging than expected.
newsitem.headline: Alumax's 96 more challenging than expected.

text.p: Alumax Inc reported lower third quarter operating profits due to declining aluminum prices and said industry conditions have become more challenging than almost anybody anticipated at the beginning of the year.
Still, it added, "many industry observers hope to see gradual improvements in aluminum consumption and pricing into 1997 and beyond, especially with even a moderate recovery in the European markets."
Alumax's third-quarter net profits rose to $52.4 million, or $1.10 per share, from $43.0 million, or $0.90, in 1995.
It said the latest quarter included an after-tax gain of $36.7 million, or $0.81 per share, on the sale of certain fabricated products businesses.

Earnings from operations in the third quarter were $44.4 million on sales of $809.1 million and shipments of 261,900 metric tonnes. This compares with earnings from operations of $91.0 million on sales of $767.7 million and shipments of 249,200 tonnes in the third quarter of 1995.
"Increased Alumax revenues and shipments in 1996 are substantially related to our growing extrusions business," the company said.

"Lower 1996 operating results, however, are mainly attributable to lower aluminum prices and to higher raw materials costs. In addition, higher total cost and expense levels this year reflect the expanded volume from our extrusion operations due to the acquisition of Cressona Aluminum Company in January.

"Earnings in the latest quarter were also affected by a seven percent decline in shipments versus the second quarter, principally in primary aluminum, and the need to reduce the carrying value of certain fabricated products business inventories by $3.1 million pretax."
